articleTitle: Tailored Raspberry Pi 3B+ Software for the Implementation of Hardware Security Primitives Based on Commercial Off-the-Shelf Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The Raspberry Pi 3B+ is a well-known single-board computer that can be used to implement and test a number of hardware security primitives suitable for Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) devices. However, the software that implements and tests these primitives is rarely made fully available as open-source code. In this work, we present and discuss open-source software for the Raspberry Pi that enables cryptographic applications using COTS hardware. In particular, we discuss the software utilised for the implementation of a Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) based on the retention characteristics of the Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) of a Raspberry Pi 3B+, as well as a kernel for the same board that allows for the implementation of a True Random Number Generator (TRNG) based on a COTS Resistive Random Access Memory (ReRAM) module.

articleTitle: Advancing Urban Transit: Gepard and CAR projects - Innovations in Trolleybus Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The Gepard project in Gdynia, Poland, revolutionized the city's trolleybus network with the introduction of "Trolleybus 2.0" vehicles and an innovative charging system. "Trolleybus 2.0" vehicles combine features of traditional trolleybuses and electric buses boasting traction batteries for autonomous driving and dual legal approval. Statistical analysis of energy consumption informed the development of a hybrid charging concept, balancing overhead contact line (OHL) coverage with additional fast charging stations. This hybrid In Motion Charhing (IMC) system reduces costs while ensuring reliable operation, even in adverse weather conditions. Moreover, as part of the CAR project, a fast charging station for trolleybuses was constructed, allowing for the additional extension of trolleybus routes.

articleTitle: Design and testing of low-cost portable magnetometer for consumer applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This paper investigates the performances of two low-cost commercial magnetometer devices QMC5883L and BMM150 for possible usage in consumer applications such as portable systems or unmanned aerial vehicles. Tested modules are presented in more detail and the special systems for data acquisition, based on commercial STM32 device, as well as system for magnetic field generation are designed and explained. Magnetometers module are tested in the controlled laboratory conditions using Helmholtz coils for different magnetic fields strengths. Measured results from both of the tested modules are presented and analyzed, followed with the discussion on more appropriate applications for each. It is shown that QMC5883L provides more reliable results for the low magnetic field measuring, while the BMM150 performs more accurately on a broader range of fields.

articleTitle: Optimization of Immersive Audio Technologies Start-up Time in Home Theatre Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: In recent years, immersive audio technologies have revolutionized how we experience sound, offering rich and multidimensional audio experiences across various industries. However, as these technologies continue to evolve, so do user expectations, with consumers now demanding seamless integration, fast startup times, and low delays in home theater (HT) systems. This paper explores a specific optimization approach aimed at reducing startup times in HT systems. Optimization is done on the side of 3d object positioning and mixing, where conditional recalculation optimization is introduced to reduce startup times by selectively recalculating mapping matrices only when necessary, such as output speaker configuration changes. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in startup times, enhancing the overall user experience in HT environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Caching Efficiency of DSM-CC Data Carousel BIOP Messages for Android TV Broadcast Stack Virtual File System
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This study addresses the challenges of enhancing caching efficiency for DSM-CC Data Carousel BIOP messages within the Android TV Broadcast Stack Virtual File System. Digital Storage Media Command and Control (DSM-CC) protocols, crucial for managing digital storage media’s bitstream, face significant efficiency issues, especially in broadcast systems where data transmission is unidirectional. The research focuses on developing innovative approaches to optimize caching mechanisms, reducing latency, and improving performance in accessing multimedia content. By proposing a strategic caching method and a dynamic approach to manage output stream capacities, the study presents a solution that significantly mitigates the problems associated with the traditional caching of large files and the reuse of cache data. Evaluation results demonstrate the effectiveness of these approaches in enhancing system performance and reliability, highlighting their potential to contribute to the advancement of digital broadcasting technologies. This work not only lays the groundwork for future research in more adaptive and efficient caching strategies but also enhances the user experience in digital broadcasting systems.

articleTitle: An environment for orchestrating containers on a local ProxMox server
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) in a Kubernetes cluster deployed on Proxmox virtualization to optimize resource utilization. Through dynamic adjustment of pod replicas based on workload demands, HPA efficiently manages resources during varying levels of activity. Practical experimentation demonstrates the effectiveness of HPA in improving resource utilization and reducing operational overhead in local server environments. This study underscores the value of autoscaling mechanisms for enhancing the scalability and reliability of Kubernetes clusters on Proxmox.

articleTitle: A tool for detecting memory interference between AUTOSAR software components of different ASIL
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Functional safety is an important aspect in the development of safety-critical software for the automotive industry, which can be challenging to achieve due to integration of software components of different criticality on one platform. The AU-TOSAR architecture supports the development of safety-critical systems by providing safety measures and mechanisms, including mechanisms in the memory domain. This paper proposes a tool for ensuring Freedom from Interference between software components of different ASIL while verifying AUTOSAR safety mechanisms in memory domain. Tool proposed in this paper is used to analyze and verify the correct implementation of memory partitioning in a system consisting of mixed-criticality software components. By verifying the correct implementation of the memory partitioning and memory mapping mechanisms, we contribute to the correct functionality of memory partitioning mechanism and memory protection unit.

articleTitle: The Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision in Large-Scale Video Surveillance of Railway Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Video surveillance equipment has become increasingly popular in the past two decades for security and human behavior insights. However, monitoring multiple cameras increases costs and makes it difficult for operators to maintain focus. To automate this process, surveillance cameras can be integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision (CV) technologies. The project aims to enhance safety and provide a secure environment through intelligent surveillance across a large network of cameras. The system presented in this paper offers real-time monitoring based on YOLOv8 and difference detection algorithms, capable of handling live recordings from over 1000 security cameras simultaneously. Key features include intelligent event detection, allowing for the definition of regions of interest (ROI) within camera views for targeted monitoring and assigning varying priority levels to alarms. The architecture supports scalability, allowing the addition of more cameras and the parallel execution of multiple AI-based scripts for video stream analysis. In this paper, an intelligent video surveillance system is presented as an example of railway station surveillance, but the technology has a wide range of applications in different domains.

articleTitle: Combined TOF and High-Resolution Video Solution for Medical Rehabilitation of a Remote Patient while Performing a Set of Exercises
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The main goal of the project is to create a unified technological platform for medical rehabilitation by monitoring the implementation of exercises set remotely.In the proposed case, the user registers on the system portal and gets access to methodological booklet and video materials for performing a set of exercises.The patient, depending on the prescribed rehabilitation program, receives for a period of time (2-3 months) a software and hardware complex for monitoring the implementation of the set of exercises with high amplitude.The implementation of sets of exercises is carried out with automatic control using the innovation system on the base of TOF (Time of Flight) camera. It is important that the patient’s video is not transferred to the cloud infrastructure. All processing is carried out on the side of the system located in the patient destination.

articleTitle: Resistance to shock analysis of Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This paper considers the process of adapting of the trained deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models to the unpredicted structural changes (shocks) in their environments. We consider the problem of the Airport Surface Planning for several simultaneously moving flights and two different approaches to it: the decentralised assemble of agents (one agent per flight) and Dispatcher agent (one agent controlling all steps of each flight). Both approaches were developed in Deep Q-Network (DQN) framework.

articleTitle: Discovering the potential of multi-assistant architecture in a smart home system
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: In the field of smart home automation, there is currently a wide array of diverse solutions, with relatively small number of users. The idea has emerged to consolidate smaller brands within a unified environment, by branding only the applications, while using the same IoT platform in the background. However, this causes issues with the branding of smart home voice skills, since the APIs created by voice assistant providers are tailored for the use with the single brand per platform. Therefore, we propose the method to use multiple different voice assistant skills on the same cloud. This initiative has brought forth several advantages, such as the adaptation of skills for different manufacturers or types of devices, and the introduction of a freemium model where scenes can be independently acquired within a new skill. Beyond business decisions, this solution has played a role in enhancing load balancing and performance. Specifically, API calls per skill now involve fewer devices, resulting in a noticeable reduction in processing requirements.

articleTitle: Tool for image annotation in context of modern object detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: A modern approach to object detection in digital images is based on machine learning, which usually requires a significant amount of annotated data. The annotation process of images involves assigning the class and the location of the objects of interest which can be a time-consuming and tedious task. In this paper, a tool for object annotation in digital images is presented. The tool implements two interfaces: one for project management and one for object annotation in form of bounding boxes. The project management interface allows the users to define the name of the project, choose the storage location, specify the classes of objects of interest, select the project gallery and choose the structured computer format for storing the annotation files. The object annotation interface allows users to create annotations for objects of interest, visualize them, manage the created annotations, and save them in the working annotation dictionary. Users can also configure additional parameters for exporting annotation files to the disk. To further streamline the annotation process, the tool offers automatic detection of objects of interest using the YOLOv5 detector.

articleTitle: Data Channel API: Middleware for Big Data Streaming in Automotive
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) now depend on increasingly advanced sensors that include high-resolution cameras or lidars, therefore it is necessary to support the exchange of big data in real-time. At the same time, In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI) systems are also more advanced and expect a large amount of data to display. Therefore, IVI systems need the streaming of big data in real-time too. Because of these needs, both systems require a solution to the same problem. In addition, these two systems also exchange big data among themselves, so there is a need for a common solution. ADAS and IVI systems can be on different platforms, have different operating systems, and have different architectures, therefore solution need to be independent of that. This paper presents an example of middleware which enables big data exchange in real-time and its performance. The middleware is independent of architecture, operating system, and third-party software.

articleTitle: Secure work from home: An exploration of OpenZiti’s componential framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: In response to the growing demand for remote work solutions, traditional VPN encounters challenges related to security, scalability and user experience. This paper advocated for a strategy to establish secure and efficient work environments, without the limitations of traditional VPN. The proposed approach leverages OpenZiti, a zero trust overlay mesh network, to address the challenges associated with the remote work.

articleTitle: Advanced UVM-Based Verification Methodology for Consumer Electronics HW Design Evaluation and Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The rapid evolution of consumer electronics demands increasingly complex hardware devices supporting a wide range of consumer needs. Designing and verifying such solutions is becoming more challenging. This paper introduces an automated approach for assessing the efficacy of implemented digital systems. Leveraging these insights, the proposed methodology aims to guide HDL designers, enabling them to identify and rectify errors more effectively. The proposed methodology is tested on the example of a relatively simple digital design on a population of twenty designers. The achieved results expose a significant increase in performance and quality in a relatively short time interval.

articleTitle: Micro Frontend Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Our paper focuses on software architectures in web application environments, specifically their evolution in client interface development. We will focus on implementing client interfaces with Micro Frontends, which are based on the principle of microservices. We will explain how to implement this architecture and integrate multiple Micro Frontends into a single web application. Additionally, we will evaluate the efficiency and performance of Micro Frontends compared to monolithic client interfaces. Finally, we will compare the performances of the two architectures and propose an improvement to implementing Micro Frontends. Our improvement proposal will explain how Micro Frontends can be implemented to create more modular and reusable user interfaces using well-known methodologies and design patterns.

articleTitle: Design and development of an IoT based Signal Generator for Testing Equipments
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Signal generators are a class of electronic devices that are considered as a vital part of test equipment setup for various applications ranging from consumer devices to aerospace and spacecraft programs. These systems are mainly used for testing, signal tracing, debugging, troubleshooting, etc. Signal generators generate different kinds of waveform in the form of an electrical signal based on the application, and are used as a stimulus for the item being tested. In this paper, design and development of a low-cost, compact, portable and Internet of Things (IoT) based signal generator is proposed. The novel contribution of proposed work is that the expected waveforms/signals can be generated from anywhere in the world over the internet using the graphical user interface (GUI) designed for the client system. The proposed signal generator is designed using an ESP32 microcontroller and a programmable Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) IC AD9833, capable of generating several basic waveforms and modulated waveforms. The proposed system costs only $10 and can generate three basic waveforms, ten modulated waveforms up to a maximum frequency of 3MHz. The proposed system will also benefit hobbyists, students and readers to design their own low cost signal generator at home itself for testing basic systems designed as a part of a mini project or project and can also be used for virtual and remote labs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: Real-Time Distracted Driver Detection Using Nvidia Jetson Nano and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach that combines cutting-edge technology and advanced models for real-time applications. Leveraging the performance of the Nvidia Jetson Nano, alongside an integrated camera and GSM/GPS module, our innovative system demonstrates both its practicality and versatility. Specifically, by employing the YOLOv8 classification model for handling State Farm Distracted Driver Detection data which underscores its adaptability and effectiveness in this critical domain. Additionally, our research thoroughly assesses computational efficiency, exploring both hardware and software-based analysis methods. This work is a cornerstone in harnessing technology for real-world impact, merging innovation with practicality and comprehensive evaluation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Modern Methods for Surface Type Identification in RGB Image Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The rapid development of drone technology and deep learning algorithms also expands the possibilities of environmental monitoring, e.g., the search and management of water bodies. This study aims to harness these advances for the accurate identification of surface types, with a specific focus on water bodies, in RGB image data. Using a dataset comprised of aerial images captured over the Baroch Pond within a nature reserve in the Czech Republic, this study comparative to evaluate the performance of deep learning models, including U-Net, Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSPNet), and DeepLabV3, in classifying surface types. The classification accuracy is slightly over 90% for most deep learning algorithms. These results show the potential of deep learning in this area. And this is key for a number of interested parties, for example, state administration, water resource managers, farmers, and tourism industry.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Real-Time Gesture controlled Television
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Gestures are used for non-verbal or non-vocal communication in which visible bodily actions communicate particular messages. Gesture recognition has now evolved into a pivotal technology with profound real-life implications, transcending novelty to provide intuitive control interfaces, adaptable to diverse applications ranging from controlling consumer electronics to controlling on-board systems in space station. In this paper, design and development of a real-time hand gesture controlled television is proposed. A total of seventeen gestures are used for the proposed work and it can be either increased or decreased, based on the consumer appliance or application requirement. Maximum recognition accuracy of 100% is achieved with an average recognition time of 2.18ms. The proposed work can be easily extended to various other applications including consumer appliances such as washing machine, refrigerators, dishwasher, air-conditioners, etc.

articleTitle: A 20GHz Radar Receiver RF front-end with Tx-to-Rx spillover cancellation circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 20GHz radar receiver RF front-end consisting of a two-stage low-noise amplifier, a mixer, an IF amplifier, and impedance transformers. In addition, the procedure for adjusting the values of the block parameters to achieve optimal values of the system characteristics is presented. Also, cancellation methods for spillover between transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) are explained, and a circuit canceling Tx-to-Rx spillover in the IF domain is designed. The circuits were designed and simulated in the Cadence software using 65nm TSMC technology. The simulation results show a Tx-to-Rx spillover cancellation of 11.78dBc for 20MHz unwanted signal.

articleTitle: Managing IoT Data Transmission in Smart Home Environments with Zero-Knowledge Proof Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This research focuses on implementing the Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) protocol as part of IoT systems, specifically within smart home environments. The system relies on the WISE protocol for communication between physical devices and the central controller. As the system evolved, the optimization concept led to migrating the central controller’s logic to the cloud. In the latest development phase, the cloud-based central controller is utilized for data processing and analysis, leveraging the WISE protocol’s features for efficient data collection from both applications and devices. As an example of a physical device, set-top boxes are utilized for real-time transmission of critical logs for diagnostic purposes. Additionally, the WISE client enables continuous log and data collection from applications, initiating upon application initialization. This capability allows the WISE client to monitor and document potential issues or irregularities in real-time application operation. The implementation of the ZKP protocol on the cloud-based central controller facilitates secure and private communication between devices and the data collection system, without compromising sensitive information. This research explores the application of the ZKP protocol concerning the utilization of physical or logical devices within systems based on the WISE protocol, providing a secure and efficient solution for device-to-central system communication in the cloud.

articleTitle: YOLOv8 Utilization in Occupational Health and Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The field of occupational health and safety focuses on minimizing losses by preserving and protecting human and physical assets in workplaces. This discipline involves monitoring workplaces and advising management on effective strategies to prevent and reduce losses. Gaining prominence through its remarkable precision and speed, the YOLO ("You-Only-Look-Once") framework assists the progress of dependable and quick object detection in images. Integrated into security systems, live tracking of video feeds for quick identification of doubtful activities, face mask conformity and social distancing are made possible by YOLO. Moreover, YOLO models find application in surface inspection, enhancing quality control in manufacturing. This study investigates the potential of lightweight nano and small YOLOv8 architectures to detect OSHA violations on construction sites, utilizing a publicly available dataset. The results are promising, with the best model achieving a 92% precision rate. YOLOv8 demonstrates potential in enhancing safety measures by detecting safety equipment such as helmets, ensuring worker safety. Despite these possibilities, links between computer vision technology and concepts of workplace safety remain unexplored, with a limited research focus. This research contributes to bridging this gap by showcasing the effectiveness of YOLOv8 in addressing occupational safety concerns, particularly in the construction industry.

articleTitle: A Solution for Management and Administration of Smart Home Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Smart home systems nowadays are the most popular examples of IoT solutions. Since they have diverse components, a centralized point for monitoring the entire system is essential. Typically, these points manifest as client applications, providing the overview of the system. On the other hand, administrator portals are crucial in managing, configuring and overseeing of the system. From user management to device configuration, these applications ensure optimal performance. To establish successful communication between components, the MQTT protocol, widely used in IoT, executes the real-time data exchange. This article explains how our administrator application utilizes MQTT for communication within our system. Moreover, as part of the evaluation, we demonstrate the measurement of MQTT command execution duration, as well as the retrieval of corresponding responses.

articleTitle: Securing Smart City Health Services Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: In smart city environments cyber security is a major issue that must be addressed across different smart service domains while delivering quality of life for citizens. Smart healthcare is an important area that ensures quality health services delivery which is reliable and effective. Smart health is an important requirement for smart city services. To explore the nuances of smart city healthcare services, the paper presents a systematic literature review using current research. The focus of this study is to highlight the important issues surrounding s-healthcare services. There are multiple issues related to data security and privacy, since smart city infrastructures are complex and make use of multiple components in exchange of information resulting in security vulnerabilities. The use of blockchain technology in tackling the security and privacy issues in smart city healthcare are explored and analysed. The paper presents the role and importance of blockchain in healthcare, issues faced by health care services and the impact of blockchain in smart healthcare services to highlight the need for secured health information exchange in smart cities.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Handloom Saree Testing System using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Silk sarees have been a part of Indian culture for centuries and are considered as traditional attire of entire women folk in India, as every weaving cluster over 200 has its uniqueness. Silk sarees are known for their exude elegance, lustrous beauty, sophistication, luxurious feel and durability. Handloom and powerloom are the two possible ways of weaving a silk saree. Handloom sarees are softer and more resilient compared to power loom sarees, whereas powerloom sarees are stiff and do not drape well. Because of these qualities, handloom sarees are preferred over powerloom sarees, and are hence expensive. In this paper, a novel attempt is made to design a silk saree testing system using an unsupervised machine learning algorithm called k-means clustering algorithm and a supervised machine learning algorithm called Decision Tree classifier. The proposed testing system is capable of detecting whether the saree under test is woven using handloom or powerloom. Two Decision Tree classifier models are designed with their performances compared and evaluated by testing the proposed system at various silk saree stores in and around Bangalore. The proposed system will serve as a reliable objective testing method over conventional inefficient subjective testing methods, giving scope for the popularization of proposed system through authentic textile testing laboratories in India and its recognition from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) as a validated testing method. The proposed system is an outcome of a funded project with Central Silk Board under Ministry of Textiles, India. The proposed system yielded a maximum recall value of 0.92 with a response time of 81 seconds and costs only $100.

articleTitle: Societal Elements that Impact the Performance of Women Entrepreneurs in Tier-II Cities: A Study of Rohilkhand Region of Uttar Pradesh
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Globally women entrepreneurship is being increasingly accepted as one of the most laten and underestimated source of economic growth. Research on women entrepreneurs has long been understudied, both globally and in India. The current global economic crisis has drawn attention from researchers to women entrepreneurs and demonstrated their significance as economic agents. The level of an entrepreneur's society influences their level of entrepreneurial activity to some extent. This study is aimed to explore the impact of societal variable on entrepreneurship sprit among women in Tier II cities of Rohilkhand region of Uttar Pradesh. Research results indicate that family support, financial concerns and lack of infrastructure are the key obstacles faced by women entrepreneurs. Study results revealed Women entrepreneurship spirit can be impacted by societal factors. Demographic variable (education and work experience) significantly impacts the societal variables that affect the spirit of women entrepreneurship while age is an insignificant demographical variables that impact the societal variables affecting spirit of women entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: Learning Localization of Body and Finger Animation Skeleton Joints on Three-Dimensional Models of Human Bodies
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Contemporary approaches to solving various problems that require analyzing three-dimensional (3D) meshes and point clouds have adopted the use of deep learning algorithms that directly process 3D data such as point coordinates, normal vectors and vertex connectivity information. Our work proposes one such solution to the problem of positioning body and finger animation skeleton joints within 3D models of human bodies. Due to scarcity of annotated real human scans, we resort to generating synthetic samples while varying their shape and pose parameters. Similarly to the state-of-the-art approach, our method computes each joint location as a convex combination of input points. Given only a list of point coordinates and normal vector estimates as input, a dynamic graph convolutional neural network is used to predict the coefficients of the convex combinations. By comparing our method with the state-of-the-art, we show that it is possible to achieve significantly better results with a simpler architecture, especially for finger joints. Since our solution requires fewer precomputed features, it also allows for shorter processing times.

articleTitle: Use of Extended Kalman Filter in an UWB based Indoor Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Ultra-wideband wireless technology has gained a lot of attention in recent years. One of the main reasons for this is the cm order precision it offers as a solution to indoor positioning systems. As the technology has become far more available than ever, so has the motivation for an implementation of a positioning system based on UWB technology risen. This paper focuses on one such implementation, specifically focusing on the implementation and use of Extended Kalman Filter in a Time-Difference of Arrival based positioning system as the core mathematical method for estimating an object’s location. The positioning system is then tested in a real physical environment showcasing the Extended Kalman Filter as a valid choice for the core positioning algorithm.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Extracting Signposts from the Scene and Understanding Text on Them
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The level of autonomy of modern vehicles is increasing every day. The vehicle performs more and more driving tasks independently. One of these tasks is recognizing signposts and understanding the text on them. In this paper, an algorithm for this purpose was developed based on a deep learning approach, specifically using You Only Look Once (YOLO) v7 applied to the images captured by the front-view camera. The solution is tested in the PC environment and on the embedded platform Raspberry Pi 4 to examine its performance when operating in limited resources conditions. The proposed solution achieved a high level of accuracy in detecting signposts, interpreting text, and determining directions. The experimental results also show that there is room for improvement, especially in cases of partial obstruction or low image quality. Notably, testing on the Raspberry Pi 4 highlighted the need for additional optimization due to software and hardware limitations, emphasizing the importance of resource-efficient algorithms for embedded platforms.

articleTitle: Battery Cluster Reverse Logistics Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: This paper explores three primary strategies that enhance not only the deployment of battery technologies through scalability and interchangeability but also examine their significant impact on reverse logistics flows. It delves into the critical role of modular battery design, advocating for the standardization of battery size, capacity, and the integration of blockchain technology in Battery Management Systems (BMS) to ensure traceability and security. Furthermore, the study will reveal specific conditions under which the cost of Going-To-Market (GTM) strategies can align with or equal the expenses associated with battery reverse logistics, offering insights into cost-effective and sustainable battery lifecycle management.

articleTitle: Protection of CAN communication on embedded platform using symmetric encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: CAN is a communication protocol used in the automotive industry because of its reliability. Over the years, the lack of implemented security mechanisms led to various solutions for the protection of the CAN bus. In this paper, the symmetric encryption of CAN communication based on DES and AES is analyzed. The cryptographic algorithms are implemented in the C programming language and evaluated on an embedded platform based on the STM32F407 microcontroller. The evaluation of the proposed solution was carried out in terms of the execution time of the encryption and decryption process.

articleTitle: Feature extraction procedures for chronic wound tissue classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: As healthcare services become both more necessary and expensive on a daily basis, the possibility arises for the inclusion of (semi)automated machine learning based approaches for aiding healthcare professionals and, hopefully, reducing costs. The area of chronic wound management, which includes diagnostics, healing process tracking, treatment related decision-making etc., represents a prominent candidate for such applications. This paper considers a straightforward approach to the classification of different tissue types constituting chronic wounds. It delves into the merits of several different feature extraction procedures and their descriptive properties when utilised at the pixel level, with the goal of selecting simple descriptors yielding solid performance and robust model behaviour. A multifaceted comparative analysis was conducted which considered performance on data stemming from both a prosthetic model and real patients in terms of different feature extraction procedures, colour spaces and window sizes. Even though the best advice anyone can ever offer is to adapt to the data at hand, the results do point at some possible shortcuts regarding feature extraction that lead to overall good performance figures.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Network for Data Augmentation and Substitution
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The healthcare industry undergoes a transformative shift with the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in medical imaging analysis. AI algorithms, trained on extensive datasets, demonstrate accuracy comparable to medical experts, promising earlier diagnoses and improved outcomes. However, challenges in widespread AI adoption include limited access to high-quality medical datasets and concerns about data privacy. These challenges hinder progress, as existing datasets often suffer from obsolescence. Overcoming these limitations is crucial for advancing AI research in healthcare. Leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) addresses data scarcity by generating synthetic medical data that maintains essential features without compromising patient privacy. GANs present a solution to challenges related to data availability and quality, unlocking new opportunities for innovation in medical AI research and clinical practice.

articleTitle: Visual Monitoring of Mice Wellness by Tiny Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Welfare of animals is nowadays very important, especially for the ones, such as mice, employed in pre-cilincal medical research. The monitoring of their wellness is matter of strong attention and calls for automated analytical procedures. Classification, detection and key behavioural indexes of their quality life and associated well-being evaluations are currently attracting attention and efforts both from research community and the industry one. In this context, this work focused on studying visual object detection approaches, to be deployed on tiny micro-controllers, in order to achieve massive scalability at the edge, for example for mice tracking within laboratory cages, in which they live. To develop that, the usage of tiny artificial neural networks was considered mandatory. The results were achieved through the study of state of art neural architectures, followed by their optimizations for tiny micro-controllers, including post training quantization and finally deploying the models on these tiny hardware targets. The final evaluation and model selection had been conducted considering both the accuracy and the performance achieved in terms of processing rate of the images and memory consumption on the target. The results shown that "YOLOv5-fpn_175K" achieved 3.03 frames per second with a mAP(IoU=0.50:0.95) of 0.707, and be deployable on a off-the-shelf micro-controller requiring 0.74 MB of RAM and 0.35 MB of FLASH.

articleTitle: A review of the approaches for enhancing driver safety through camera-based monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Road accidents caused by human error continue to result in a rising number of serious injuries and fatalities each year. Automated Driving Assistance Systems (ADAS) offer a promising approach by continuous monitoring of drivers to promptly identify and address unsafe behaviors. A further technical challenge is solely relying on camera sensors to determine crucial human deficiencies such as drowsiness and distraction. In our research, we provide a review of relevant papers from the field of computer vision for driver monitoring. Most of these approaches rely on Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for both image processing and driver state classification. Our findings indicate that Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and CNNs consistently outperform other techniques in terms of accuracy. In conclusion, we present our perspective on the essential features that a comprehensive driver monitoring system (DMS) should include.

articleTitle: Detecting Mice Depth Shapes with Deployable Tiny Neural Networks in Small Cages
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Detecting tiny shapes, per pixel, of mammals can be challenging in small environments, such as the cages used for pre-clinical studies. There are tens of racks containing hundreds of cages in a typical installation. In such a context, this paper examined several neural models, taking into account their computational and memory complexity, to ensure that they can be deployed on tiny off-the-shelf and cheap microcontrollers. The study employed a NUCLEO board with STM32U5 connected to a time of flight sensor named VL53L8CX. This sensor generated sequences of depth frames over time. These data were collected into a hand-crafted dataset, which, following a data augmentation process, achieved a totals of 2498 samples. The models considered were: a U-Net based architecture; a hand-crafted one, called Micronet. The latter, following the post-training quantization procedure to 8 bits integer, achieved a mAP score above 86%, an inference time of 0.27 ms, a FLASH size of 1.3 KiB and a RAM usage of 0.5 KiB. These results enabled the implementation of a high-speed detector on cheap microcontroller chip.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Implementation of the UTAUT Model in Assessing Factors Influencing Consumer Loan Decisions on Online Loan Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: Online lending (pinjol) has witnessed substantial growth in Indonesia, with 101 licensed fintech peer-to-peer (P2P) lending providers as of 2023. The sector boasts 19,525,882 active loan recipient accounts, totaling 55.6 trillion Indonesian Rupiah in funding as of September 2023. While the popularity of online loans can be attributed to their convenience, speed, and lenient application requirements, they face criticism for high-interest rates. This study, employing the UTAUT methodology, aims to investigate factors influencing consumer decision-making in selecting online loans. The research examines variables such as performance expectancy (PE), effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), facilitating conditions (FC), behavioral intention (BI), and security (S). Utilizing quantitative data from a survey of 179 respondents, the study delves into the factors shaping consumer decisions in the online lending landscape in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Implementation of parallel K-means algorithm for image classification using OpenMP and MPI libraries
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: The k-means algorithm is a widely used Machine learning algorithm for clustering. This paper introduces a parallel k-means algorithm implementation for image classification. We implemented several parallel programs using OpenMP and MPI libraries and tested them on three MNIST variants datasets: MNIST, Fashion MNIST, and Extended MNIST. The algorithm parameters and scheduling methods are varied during experiments. The implementations use both libraries, run on multiple computers, and utilize all available processor cores. The proposed implementations achieve a speedup of up to 10.2 while using 12 processor cores.

articleTitle: The role of multimedia in e-commerce: An analysis of Czech e-shop websites
publicationTitle: 2024 Zooming Innovation in Consumer Technologies Conference (ZINC)
abstract: E-commerce has revolutionized the way businesses interact with consumers and emphasizes the importance of online presence and sales strategies. This study explores the evolving landscape of e-commerce and focusses on the essential role of multimedia content in increasing user engagement and satisfaction in the web application of Czech e-shops. Multimedia elements, including audio, video, animation, and interactive functions, offer unique opportunities for attracting consumers and influencing their purchase decisions. The study analyses data from surveys conducted between Czech online shopping platforms to determine the impact of multimedia integration on user perception of website design and overall satisfaction. The study examines the decision tree algorithm as tools for classifying the attributes of electronic shops and predicting user perceptions of graphic interest. Despite the challenges of data complexity and classification accuracy, the insights generated from these analyses provide valuable guidance to companies looking to optimize their multimedia strategies and improve consumer e-commerce experiences. It is assumed that the user’s first impression is closely related to the presence and quality of multimedia and content elements in the user interface of a website. However, based on the results of the survey, it turns out that while the user’s first impression is closely related to the evaluation of the graphical attractiveness of the e-shop, the presence of the specific observed multimedia and content elements on the website’s user interface is not significant.
